title: The imec Report: Scaling Optical Interconnects For The AI Era
gist: imec opinion piece laying out a three-stage optical interconnect roadmap for AI: pluggables (1.6T now, 3.2T by decade end) needing new electro-optic materials like LiNbO3/LiTaO3, DSP-free co-packaged optics with broad deployment from 2027/2028, and wafer-stacked 3D integrated optics (OIO3D) with proof-of-concepts in 3-5 years and commercialization in 5-10. It cites concrete targets (400G lanes, ~1Tbps/mm, 5 to 3 pJ/bit for CPO; >10Tbps/mm, sub-1pJ/bit, <100ns for 3D) and imec device firsts.

insights.claim: Energy-efficient electrical links are generally limited to millimeter-scale reach; at longer distances and higher lane rates power rises sharply, thermals worsen and signal integrity degrades, making electrical I/O a key barrier to scaling AI systems.
insights.speaker: Imene Jadli
insights.so_what: Underpins the structural demand shift from copper to optics across the AI data center, benefiting photonics suppliers.
insights.quote: electrical I/O is rapidly becoming a key barrier to scaling next-generation AI and machine learning systems

insights.claim: The author argues incremental innovation will not suffice and the optical roadmap must progressively move optics from the front panel into the package and ultimately into the wafer stack.
insights.speaker: Imene Jadli
insights.so_what: Value migrates toward advanced packaging, hybrid bonding and foundry photonics over time, away from standalone module assembly.
insights.quote: progressively brings optics closer to the silicon – from the front panel, into the package, and ultimately firmly integrated into the wafer stack

insights.claim: Micro-transfer printing places thin-film materials on SiPho wafers without the material waste, post-bonding complexity and cost of conventional wafer bonding, though scaling to high-volume manufacturing still needs work.

insights.claim: Heavy DSP used in pluggables adds power and latency that become problematic for short-reach chip-to-chip AI links, which need intrinsically clean low-BER channels; this is what drives adoption of fast-and-narrow co-packaged optics.
insights.speaker: Imene Jadli
insights.so_what: CPO adoption is a headwind for DSP chip vendors in short-reach AI scale-up links.

insights.claim: CPO shrinks the electrical path from several centimeters in pluggables to a few millimeters or less, improving signal integrity and latency without power-hungry DSP.
insights.speaker: Imene Jadli
insights.so_what: Explains why switch and accelerator vendors are moving optics into the package.

insights.claim: imec's CPO (OIO2.5D) targets include scaling optical engines from 1.6T/3.2T to 6.4T and 12.8T, 400Gbps lanes, bandwidth density near 1Tbps per millimeter, and efficiency of 5pJ/bit trending to 3pJ/bit.

insights.claim: Integration complexity is CPO's defining challenge, requiring co-design of PICs, EICs, switch ASICs, fiber coupling, thermal management and advanced packaging such as 2.5D interposers, TSVs, FO-WLP and hybrid bonding.

insights.claim: Early CPO systems will use external laser sources to ease thermal management and laser reliability near hot ASICs, at the cost of higher laser power, more packaging complexity and extra fibers and connectors.

insights.so_what: Near-term CPO creates a market for high-power external laser modules and fiber connectivity.

insights.claim: In October 2025 imec demonstrated a beyond-110GHz C-band GeSi electro-absorption modulator achieving net 400Gbps per lane, compatible with 300mm CMOS SiPho platforms.
insights.speaker: Imene Jadli
insights.so_what: A CMOS-compatible 400G-lane modulator lowers the manufacturing barrier for next-gen optical engines.

insights.claim: Key CPO building blocks are moving into pilot lines, supply-chain preparation and wafer-level services, with broad large-scale CPO deployment expected from 2027/2028.

insights.claim: Over the next decade, chip-to-chip optical links are expected to need bandwidth densities approaching or above 10Tbps/mm, energy well below 1pJ/bit and latency under 100ns, beyond what advanced CPO can deliver.
insights.speaker: Imene Jadli
insights.so_what: Implies CPO is a transitional architecture, with long-term value accruing to wafer-level photonic integration.
insights.quote: These targets extend beyond what even advanced CPO architectures can achieve.
insights.locator: 3D integrated optics (OIO3D): The next frontier

insights.claim: OIO2.5D places photonic and electronic dies side by side on a silicon interposer using Cu hybrid bonding, targeting 8-32Tbps engines with DSP-free 32-64Gbps lanes and 8-32 WDM wavelengths, aiming at 2Tbps/mm and about 2pJ/bit.
insights.speaker: Imene Jadli
insights.so_what: Wide-and-slow WDM architectures favor multi-wavelength laser and filter suppliers.

insights.claim: OIO3D stacks photonic layers directly above or below compute silicon using die-to-wafer and wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding, with on-wafer laser integration such as quantum-dot GaAs-on-Si explored in EU Chips Act pilot lines.
insights.speaker: Imene Jadli
insights.so_what: Wafer-to-wafer bonding and on-chip lasers are long-dated enablers to watch.

insights.claim: 3D integrated optics is still in early R&D, with first proof-of-concept demonstrators expected in three to five years and wider commercialization on a five- to ten-year horizon.
insights.speaker: Imene Jadli
insights.so_what: Investors should not price near-term revenue for in-wafer optics.
